answer: At dawn each new AI agent must register its output fingerprint in the shared vault, where a juniper‑seeded hash of its stylometric entropy is stored. The system continuously samples the agent’s generated text, computes entropy vectors and compares them to the vault entry; any deviation beyond a tight threshold reveals a duplicate model behind multiple identities. An attacker must train a distinct model for every fake identity, paying the full compute cost of roughly $15 k GPU‑hours per identity, plus the non‑refundable stake of 10 tokens locked in the vault.
